transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You are lost, aren't you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My name is Salim. I came looking for my brother Omar who vanished near this place, and I need to know what this village is.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower your voice; sound travels strangely across this stone, and names don't settle long near this well.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I hear you, but what is this place, and who lives in those houses?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: This is a jinn village. Keep your distance from the houses and don't lay a hand on the dark water. They do not welcome the living who wander in uninvited.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I won't go near it or the water. Just tell me how to stand without angering them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I can't leave this fountain, not even a step; I've been bound to it longer than I can count. Long enough that words slip mid-sentence, even my own name some mornings.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then help me before it takes more from you. Tell me how they live.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The longer I stand here the thinner my thoughts become; fear makes that thinning faster, so don't feed it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Tell me who listens and who decides.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Eyes watch from those dark houses, and staring back is taken as defiance. Pride angers them faster than fear.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared Omar to come close one night. I mocked his fear. When he didn't return, I followed the shame here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then listen plain: there are watchers who hold the edges, listeners who drift near the fountain, and above them sits a will that hates being handled.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't handle it. Just tell me how to stand so they don't turn on me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't count the houses. Don't claim what isn't yours. And never speak the king's name as though it is something you can wield — that kind of certainty draws the worst attention.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't. Omar wouldn't have known any of this.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: If they press you for a name and it falters, admit it. Clinging too hard to a fading word angers them more than letting it go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll admit it and keep my eyes low.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Helping you thins me; my jaw's shaking and my head aches. The surface is restless because they notice I'm speaking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I see it. I'm sorry, but please finish.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't bargain, don't praise, don't mock their shapes. They punish control more than ignorance.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I know which place is mine?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: If a watcher fixes you, lower your eyes. If a listener drifts close, answer short. If no one claims you, wait without fidgeting.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then give me the words before they decide anything.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It costs me to say them; my head won't stop throbbing. When I speak, you repeat once and only once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm ready.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give. My hands won't stop shaking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am still here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't waste them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when you feel yourself slipping. Use the second only when the pale hands reach you — not before. The order matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Answer only what you are asked. If a memory slips, don't chase it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Thank you, Hanash.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Hold to your breath and your footing. Don't waste what I gave you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't.
